description: Somos Young Avengers, equipo de Sistemas del Instituto Tecnológico de Cuautla, Morelos. Vamos por el reto Abandonados pero no olvidados: contar las historias de los robots y naves que la NASA dejó en la Luna y Marte, como Opportunity y Spirit. Haremos un museo virtual interactivo. Buscamos diseño, front-end, investigación y video.
summary:
We created a fun web video game for primary school kids, where they can play, explore, and learn about space.

In our game, kids can interact with 3 real NASA spacecraft in 3D, rotate them, zoom in, and click on them to discover their story. Each ship tells, in simple and fun words, what its mission was, how it got lost in space, and why we should not forget it.

The game has colorful visuals, easy controls, big buttons, and short stories so children from 6 to 12 years old can play without help. It runs directly in the web browser, without installing anything.

We use real 3D models and textures from the official NASA 3D catalog, optimized in Blender and built as an interactive web game in Godot and exported to HTML5.

Our goal is to make space history exciting, easy to understand, and unforgettable for the next generation of explorers.
details:
WHAT IS IT?
Our project is a fun web video game for primary school kids (6 to 12 years old). Players can interact with 3 real NASA spacecraft in 3D, rotate them, zoom in, and click on them to discover their story: what was their mission, how they got lost in space, and why we should not forget them.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
1. We download 3D models of real NASA spacecraft from the official free NASA 3D Resources catalog, with real textures from real missions.
2. We optimize the models in Blender using Decimate to reduce polygons, and Python scripts to scale, center and apply textures, so they run fast in a browser.
3. We build the game in Godot Engine using GDScript: easy controls, big buttons, camera movement around the ships, click to open fun fact cards, sounds and colorful visuals.
4. We export the game to HTML5 / WebAssembly, so it works as a web page. No installation needed, it works on school computers, tablets and phones.

WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS?
- Makes space history easy, fun and unforgettable for kids.
- Kids learn by playing, not by reading long texts.
- It is free, accessible and works in any browser.
- It rescues forgotten missions and shows that even lost missions teach us something.

EXPECTED IMPACT:
We want children in primary schools to get excited about science and space, to know real NASA missions, and to feel like future explorers. Teachers can use it in class as an interactive activity.

TOOLS USED:
NASA 3D Resources catalog, Blender + Python, Godot Engine + GDScript, HTML5 / WebAssembly, GitHub Pages / itch.io for publishing.

WHY IS IT CREATIVE?
Instead of a boring museum or a text page, we turned lost spacecraft into game characters with simple, funny stories for kids. We mix real NASA data with play, colors and interaction.

WHAT FACTORS DID WE CONSIDER?
Easy language for kids, short texts, big buttons, bright colors, safe content without violence, fast loading for school computers, and no installation.
